source.title: "Train classical, deploy quantum" requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: S. Raj; Natansh Mathur; A. Perdomo-Ortiz

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether converged moment-matching losses imply generalization and finds they can fail to track it, with strong dependence on model structure, dataset, initialization, and training settings. This refines the generalization claim for generative models rather than the specified natural-label classification setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own empirical benchmark, scaling and ablation results, plus theoretical constructions. Results cited from prior work are not extracted. Rows cover the reported conditions and metrics most directly bearing on the generalization gap; the extensive per-ε tables and diagnostic plots are not exhaustively transcribed.
record.test_reason: The study tests generalization in generative distribution learning through coverage, forward KL and moment losses. None of V1–V8 concerns this behavior: capacity sweeps do not test classifier width beyond interpolation, and loss-ranking comparisons do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. Its own results therefore test none of the supplied claim versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that converged moment-matching losses do not reliably rank generative performance and that the train-classical, deploy-quantum workflow requires evaluation through deployed samples. Their sparse-minimizer theorem concerns bounded-capacity moment losses, not the full characteristic population MMD. They advocate feeding sampling results back into training and incorporating task constraints into model structure.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks quantum and classical generative models using moment losses, likelihood losses, sampling-based coverage and forward KL on designed valid sets. The claim versions concern classification of natural labels, while this work concerns generative distribution learning.
record.method_sensitivity: Coverage changes with dataset, model family and task structure; IQP results change substantially with initialization on genomic data, modestly with initialization on cardinality data, and with training objective. Increasing IQP gate count or generator weight does not improve coverage in reported sweeps; magic-FBM training settings change genomic coverage. Kernel bandwidth sweep leaves IQP coverage near its random-bit baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Bounded-capacity moment losses admit exact sparse minimizers with poor coverage and infinite forward KL. At N=12, the order-two construction has approximately zero truncated loss and coverage 0.07. The theorem does not apply to the full characteristic population MMD, whose unique minimizer is the target.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching a bounded set of moments does not certify generative distribution coverage or small forward KL; an empirical full-MMD minimum can also memorize the training distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Across model families, low eval MMD does not reliably rank coverage or forward KL. At N=16, IQP and TNBM cover approximately 0.17 and 0.52, respectively, despite comparably small MMD values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low moment-matching discrepancy alone does not reliably identify the better generator in these benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing IQP capacity does not improve coverage; magic-FBM depth changes coverage little. Transformer coverage rises then plateaus, RNN coverage plateaus or slightly decreases, and TNBM coverage rises then falls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capacity effects on generative coverage depend on architecture and training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Marginal-matching initialization raises genomic IQP coverage from 0.014 to 0.112, while cardinality coverage changes from 0.136 to 0.170.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization can materially affect moment-trained generative coverage, with the effect depending on the dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact likelihood improves IQP coverage from 0.17 to 0.20 at N=16 and from 0.09 to 0.14 at N=20, while substantial gaps to classical generators persist.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the training objective improves the tested IQP generator's coverage and forward KL without closing its performance gap.

record.problems: The benchmark uses designed application-inspired datasets and known valid sets, not natural-label classification. The largest-system results use state-vector simulation and finite query budgets; some reported sweeps use a single run. Reported seed counts are three or five for main benchmarks, and selected appendix comparisons use single runs. Theoretical sparse minimizer statements concern distributions and do not establish that the tested circuit families realize those minimizers.
record.rows_left_out: Not all per-ε cardinality tables, per-model Table I values, model-family diagnostic plots, and per-bandwidth figure points were transcribed. The remaining benchmark entries are in Tables VI–XI and Figures 6–16; omitted values either repeat the same model-by-condition pattern or are secondary diagnostics. All claim-version statuses are not_tested, so no version-specific rows were required.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Classifier width beyond zero training error, convergence, and subsequent test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning, switching, and decoupled weight decay.

Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and recipe changes that recover performance. Different batch sizes accompany different autoregressive model sizes, without an isolated batch-size comparison.
Dropout's effect on classifier held-out error, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, classifier generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Influence-defined memorization, targeted training-example removal, retraining, and test accuracy relative to random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address different constructs; this does not invalidate the reported generative results. No version-specific missing results or verdicts are warranted. The study's generalization terminology and capacity sweeps do not make it a T5 test of the supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare fitting random labels with generalizing on natural labels in classification.
It does not test widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks past an interpolation threshold.
It does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Although it reports Adam training, it does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or test optimizer generalization differences.
It does not vary batch size or compare large-batch and small-batch training.
Dropout appears as an architecture hyperparameter for transformers, but the study does not test its effect on held-out error.
It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures with sharpness.
It does not remove influential memorized training examples and retrain.
